input: # JSON5 IdentifierName keys may spell a character as a \uXXXX
# UnicodeEscapeSequence; the key's VALUE is the decoded text.
# An escape cannot smuggle an otherwise-illegal character into an
# identifier (ES5.1 7.6): a digit or ZWNJ at the start, a hyphen or
# space anywhere, a non-\u escape, a truncated escape, and escaped
# UTF-16 surrogate halves are all rejected.
# A raw astral character is a letter to a reader that walks code POINTS,
# and an unpaired high surrogate to one that walks UTF-16 code units.
# ES5.1 7.6 makes an IdentifierStart a UnicodeLetter, so a character
# outside the Basic Multilingual Plane opens a key when its category is
# a letter one. U+1D49C MATHEMATICAL SCRIPT CAPITAL A is Lu, U+10400
# DESERET CAPITAL LETTER LONG I is Lu and U+20000 CJK UNIFIED IDEOGRAPH
# is Lo, and a JavaScript engine accepts each of the three as a variable
# name. These rows were a divergence until 2026-09-21: canonical
# TypeScript asked isIdentifierStart(src[i]) and got back one UTF-16
# CODE UNIT, so the high surrogate, in no letter category, refused the
# key. The canonical text check now reads a code POINT and all three
# runtimes agree, which is what these rows hold it to.
# The controls, so that reading a code point does not become "accept any
# astral character". U+1F600 GRINNING FACE is So: not an IdentifierStart
# and not an IdentifierPart either. U+1D7CE MATHEMATICAL BOLD DIGIT ZERO
# is Nd: an IdentifierPart, so legal in a LATER position and not as the
# first character, exactly as `0` itself is.
